findings.issue: getTeamPage duplicates the 'find default variety, fetch Pokémon, sort types by slot' resolution already implemented in getPokemonPage (pokedex.ts:217); a third variant of the type-slot rule lives in the home page's inverted index (pokedex.ts:153-164)
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared helper, e.g. getDefaultPokemon(species) and/or typesForSpecies(id), and have all three loaders call it

findings.issue: Team list re-implements CardList's grid (identical repeat(auto-fill, minmax(var(--card-min-width),1fr)) CSS) and hand-builds card objects inline at lines 36-37
findings.suggestion: Reuse CardList (accepting a per-item snippet or children for the Remove button), or at least move the grid into CardList via a slot so card layout changes in one place

findings.issue: Card.hidden exists only for the ability page, and PokemonCard.svelte:17 renders 'Hidden ability' — ability-specific knowledge embedded in the shared card component/type; cardsFor's extra callback (pokedex.ts:132) also exists solely for it
findings.suggestion: Keep the shared Card generic: have the ability page append the note via CardList's children slot, or accept an optional annotation snippet prop on PokemonCard

findings.issue: TeamMember duplicates Card's fields plus a redundant typeNames array parallel to types
findings.suggestion: Define TeamMember as Card & { typeNames: string[] } (or derive typeNames from types in the component) to keep one card shape

findings.issue: getPokemonList does filtering, pagination and card construction inline in one 46-line function, making a new filter (or the hypothetical sort-by-name) a multi-point edit across +page.server.ts, this function and +page.svelte's href()
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is given the size, but a small filters-parse helper shared by the route and the loader would reduce the three-place filter plumbing

summary: A genuinely easy codebase to edit: one organized data module, narrow shared view-model types, small single-purpose components, and modern Svelte 5/SvelteKit idioms throughout. The reference-derived card lists all funnel through one mapping (cardsFor) and data-source concerns are fully centralized in api.ts, so the highest-frequency fixes land in one place. The team feature is where editability degrades: it copied the default-Pokémon resolution and CardList's layout instead of extracting seams, and the abilities feature leaks a flag into the shared Card component.
